profile.address: 2299, West Obispo Avenue, Gilbert, Maricopa County, Arizona, 85233
profile.reading:
The building at 2299 West Obispo Avenue in Gilbert, Arizona is a two-story, roughly 180,480-square-foot commercial property built in 1997 on about 13 acres, known in Phoenix-area commercial real estate as the El Dorado Tech Center. GoDaddy, the web-hosting and domain-registration company headquartered nearby in Tempe, has occupied the building since September 2017 under a 10-year lease running through August 2027, and public records identify it as GoDaddy's largest operational site in Arizona.

County incentive filings and the Town of Gilbert's economic-development office describe the site's current role clearly: it operates as a 24-hour customer service center, not a leased colocation data center. In late 2017, GoDaddy and Gilbert struck a roughly $15 million capital-improvement and lease-retention agreement, expanding the space from about 165,000 to 180,480 square feet and committing to retain about 1,364 direct jobs (an estimated 1,788 counting indirect effects), in exchange for local incentives tied to a projected $1.53 billion, ten-year economic impact and $80.5 million in annual personal income for area residents. Renovation began in fall 2017 and proceeded in eight phases so as not to disrupt the center's round-the-clock staffing, with completion targeted for early 2020.

Architecturally, the renovation -- led by design firm SmithGroup -- converted what its own project description calls a formerly dim, crowded space that had originally served as a data center into open, daylit office and call-center space: a double-height central stair connecting the two floors, new windows for outdoor sightlines, an expanded cafe with food-truck access, dedicated training and meeting rooms, and amenity spaces including a technology-free relaxation area. That detail -- an original data-center shell repurposed into call-center office space -- is notable for a building carried in data center registries: the most recent public reporting describes active daily use here as customer-support operations, not as server or colocation infrastructure.

In March 2018, ownership of the building itself changed hands: Arch Street Capital Advisors, acting for Dubai-based BMA International, bought the fully leased property from Everest Holdings for $39 million ($216 per square foot), with GoDaddy remaining the sole tenant throughout. No current public source describes IT power capacity, server-floor square footage, or a colocation offering at this address.

reading.body:
This facility does not qualify as an AI-capable data center campus. The building at 2299 West Obispo Avenue in Gilbert, Arizona is a 180,480-square-foot commercial property that operated originally as a data center but has been renovated since 2017 into a customer service and call-center operation. County filings and the town's economic development office document its current use as a 24-hour customer support center, not as a leased colocation facility or compute infrastructure site. The renovation, completed around 2020, converted server space into open office and call-center areas with windows, common spaces, and training rooms.

The published specifications contain no IT power capacity, server-floor square footage, or colocation offering for this address. The facility appears in data center registries as a legacy entry from its original purpose, but no current public source describes active compute infrastructure or power allocation. A Wikipedia article mentions GoDaddy operates a separate 270,000-square-foot data center in Phoenix, Arizona, roughly 20 to 25 miles away, but this cannot be confirmed as the same site.

In Arizona's published landscape, this facility holds no measurable position. The state has 56 mapped data center facilities and 512 MW of published capacity across 4 sites, but this Gilbert location publishes no megawatt figure and does not rank among the four facilities with disclosed power. For a reader evaluating AI-relevant infrastructure, this campus does not belong in the analysis.
